extracted.intended_audience: patent applicants and practitioners seeking expedited (Track One) examination at the USPTO
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance on using the USPTO's Track One prioritized patent examination program, covering eligibility (application types), timing and filing requirements, fees, annual limits, and expected performance (time to final disposition).

rubrics_metrics.name: Annual limit on accepted prioritized examination requests
rubrics_metrics.description: Effective July 8, 2025, the USPTO increased the limit on the number of prioritized examination requests that it may accept in a fiscal year from 15,000 to 20,000.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The page references the final rule published July 8, 2025 and prior Federal Register notices (2011, 2019, 2021). Up-to-date statistics for Track One are available on the USPTO Dashboard.

rubrics_metrics.name: Eligible application types
rubrics_metrics.description: The USPTO offers Track One for prioritized examination of your utility and plant patent applications.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Track One is explicitly limited to utility and plant patent applications (i.e., not design applications per the provided text).

rubrics_metrics.name: Timing for requesting prioritized examination
rubrics_metrics.description: Prioritized examination is available for a fee at the time of filing an original utility or plant application.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Request must be made at the time of filing an original application. (The page also links to a Prioritized Examination Request Form PTO/AIA/424 and related FAQs and guides.)

rubrics_metrics.name: Fee requirement
rubrics_metrics.description: Prioritized examination is available for a fee.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The fee is required when requesting Track One at the time of filing; the page points to the request form and related guidance for fee details (amounts and payment instructions found via the linked resources).

rubrics_metrics.name: RCE (Request for Continued Examination) eligibility for Track One
rubrics_metrics.description: A single request for prioritized examination may be granted for a Request for Continued Examination (RCE) in a plant or utility application.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This indicates that Track One status can be applied to one RCE in an eligible application—see the 'Prioritized Examination (RCE) Final Rule' notice (Dec. 19, 2011) for details and limitations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Expected elapsed-time performance metric
rubrics_metrics.description: Track One will allow you to get a final disposition within about twelve months.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This is the program's performance expectation; applicants should consult USPTO statistics and guidance for observed outcomes and for exceptions or caveats.

rubrics_metrics.name: Process differences from accelerated examination
rubrics_metrics.description: Track One gives your application special status with fewer requirements than the current accelerated examination program and without having to perform a pre-examination search.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applicants who previously considered accelerated examination should note Track One's reduced procedural burdens—review the Frequently Asked Questions and rule notices for specific requirement differences.
